thread:
Alex: Heads-up — I'm taking over primary for the overnight window (00:00 - 08:00 UTC). Maya will be secondary. Leaving notes below for potential coverage gaps and escalation routing.

Maya: thanks — added to my calendar. any known flaky services tonight?

Alex: nothing current in pagerduty, but last night we saw intermittent KV cache evictions on gpu-pool-2. If latency > 250ms p50 for > 3m, treat as priority-2 and page SRE.

Sahil: quick pointer — runbook link: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/inference-kv-cache. It has a quick triage checklist and the recovery k8s command.

Oncall Bot: Incident created: INC-48921 (possible KV eviction spike). Triage score: 4/10. Paging rules apply.

Alex: copying the key escalation steps we agreed in playbook:

```
- Sev1 (customer impact, >30% failed requests OR traffic drop >20%): page @sre-lead + @eng-oncall-primary + @pager oncall 1st escalation
- Sev2 (degraded latency >250ms p50 or error increase >5pp for >5m): page @eng-oncall-primary and @sre-rotation
- Sev3 (minor spike, transient <5m): Slack alert only, add to postmortem if recurs
- Always escalate to on-call lead if mitigation >30m without rollback
```

Maya: if we need to escalate to external Pager (phone) — do we call ops-team or the duty manager? I recall phone-only for Sev1 after 5m.

Alex: correct — phone escalation kicks in for Sev1 after 5m and for unresolved Sev2 after 30m. Duty manager contact is in the runbook metadata.

Zara: re: primary/secondary handoff checklist — please ensure the following before leaving: token rotation status, outstanding deploys, ongoing incidents with open actions, and any scheduled autoscale windows. I dropped a short checklist here: https://redwood-internal/handbooks/handoff-checklist

Sahil: also add config snippet we use to route traffic in a degraded region. paste into k8s job if we need quick reroute: 

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: routing-overrides
data:
  prefer_region: "us-west-2"
  fallback_tier: "compatible-quantized"
```

Alex: for tonight specifically — priority routing: if gpu-pool-2 has >10% 5xx over 5m, switch requests for the affected model to gpu-pool-1 with throttle 0.7 and enable quantized fallback. Runbook has the exact cli: `rctl reroute --from gpu-pool-2 --to gpu-pool-1 --throttle 0.7 --fallback quantized-v2`

Maya: noted. If we trigger that, can someone monitor cost delta? Want to avoid billing surprises.

Alex: I'll watch cost dashboard and add a short note to the incident. If cost > $200/hr increase we alert finance on-call (contact in runbook).

IncidentBot: Reminder — please update the incident ticket with mitigation steps and attach any logs/samples.

Maya: one more: for customer-impact calls, we have a triage template. Quick copy here:
- summary of impact
- affected models/services
- mitigation in place
- expected time to resolution
- next steps & owner

Zara: thanks. I'm around until 00:30 UTC for warm handoff. after that I'll be reachable by DM if needed.

Alex: perfect. I'll start a short shift note after my first check-in at 00:05 with p50/p95 latency and page counts. Everyone else — please ack if you see anything unusual. :thumbsup:

Maya: ack.

Sahil: ack.

Oncall Bot: Shift handoff recorded: primary=Alex, secondary=Maya, handover_time=1747890123.

Alex: closing the thread — will reopen if anything pops.
